name: Little Kulala
positioning: Solar-powered Wilderness desert camp on the private Kulala Wilderness Reserve, with its own gate to the Sossusvlei dunes and Dead Vlei
best_for: Travelers who want early, direct access to Sossusvlei and Dead Vlei
Couples wanting suites with a private pool and a rooftop for sundowners
Guests who want desert walks, drives, e-bikes and stargazing on one fully inclusive rate

facts.text: Little Kulala lies on 27,000 hectares of the Kulala Wilderness Reserve.
The area lies in the south of the Namib Desert, in the Namib-Naukluft National Park, where salt and clay pans are surrounded by high red dunes.
Some 30 years ago Wilderness pushed to protect the landscape, returning the former goat farmland to its natural state.
The camp's decor echoes the local geology, reflecting the surrounding grey and pink limestone.
Each suite has a rooftop for private sundowners and suppers.
Activities include nature walks and drives, e-bikes and low-impact quad bikes.
Desert-adapted wildlife includes ostriches, springbok, gemsbok, black-backed jackals, bat-eared foxes, perhaps an aardwolf, and Namibia's endemic dune lark.
Guided stargazing through the constellations is offered.
Menus highlight indigenous produce such as Namibian dates, eembe fruit, venison, millet and local beans.
There is a wine cellar for a private dinner for two.
The fully inclusive rate covers accommodation, all meals, twice-daily camp activities, park fees, laundry and local drinks, except premium imported brands and champagne.

highlights.text: An exclusive-use gate gives Little Kulala guests direct access to the Sossusvlei dunes and Dead Vlei.
Each suite has its own private pool.
A roll-out bed on the suite's shaded deck can be used for a siesta or a night's sleep outdoors.
Guests can climb the 300-metre red dunes and look over the Namib Sand Sea World Heritage Site.
After-dark walks reveal creatures such as scorpions glowing under UV light.

considerations.text: The camp is in a remote part of Namibia; the quickest way to reach it is by light aircraft with Wilderness Air.
Hot air balloon flights launch at dawn from near Sesriem, about 45 minutes from camp, and must be booked well in advance; they are subject to weather.
